title: A Blackout on the Night Train
briefing: As the luxury Alpine Express entered the deep mountain tunnel, the lights failed across all carriages. In the three minutes of darkness, a diplomat's encrypted dispatch case was stolen. Five passengers were in the saloon car, and one of them is guilty.

suspects.name: Baroness Von Brandt
suspects.publicStatement: I remained seated in my plush booth throughout the blackout.

suspects.name: Captain Henrik Lind
suspects.publicStatement: I was checking ticket manifests in the guard cabin.
suspects.background: Experienced railway official with fifteen years on this route.

suspects.name: Greta Weiss
suspects.publicStatement: I was typing interview notes on my portable typewriter.

suspects.name: Stefan Novak
suspects.publicStatement: I was inspecting the auxiliary diesel generator.
suspects.background: Locomotive mechanic familiar with every switchboard.

suspects.name: Oliver Sterling
suspects.publicStatement: I was clearing crystal wine glasses in the pantry.

clues.title: Crushed Saloon Velvet Cushion
clues.description: Footprint impressions on the velvet booth cushion prove someone climbed over the partition during the blackout.
clues.insight: Contradicts the Baroness's claim that she never left her seat.

clues.title: Guard Cabin Telemetry Stamp
clues.description: Automated radio sign-offs verify Captain Lind was logged into railway communications at 11:33 PM.
clues.insight: Exonerates Captain Lind by establishing his presence in the radio cabin.

clues.title: Typewriter Carbon Ribbon
clues.description: The fresh mechanical ribbon on Greta's typewriter shows text typed throughout the tunnel darkness.
clues.insight: Corroborates Greta's alibi of continuous typing at the window table.

clues.title: Dropped Brass Switch Key
clues.description: A brass electrical key dropped near the breaker box, belonging to engineer Novak.
clues.insight: Suggests sabotage, but Novak dropped it while legitimately repairing the fault.

clues.title: Attendant Corkscrew Latch
clues.description: A silver service corkscrew belonging to Oliver found tangled in luggage netting.
clues.insight: Casts suspicion on the attendant, but was left when serving wine earlier.

clues.title: Journalist Smear Notebook
clues.description: Notes detailing allegations against the Ambassador, creating suspicion of investigative theft.
clues.insight: Demonstrates journalistic interest, but physical evidence clears Greta.

clues.title: Gold-Tipped Walking Cane Scratches
clues.description: Distinctive brass scratches on the luggage rack matching the tip of the Baroness's bespoke cane.
clues.insight: Directly places the Baroness's personal walking stick at the crime scene.

clues.title: Pawned Embassy Dossier Memo
clues.description: A carbon draft listing specific treaty clauses that would collapse the Baroness's railway consortium.
clues.insight: Establishes a critical existential motive to intercept the treaty papers.

clues.title: Hidden Luggage Leather Lining
clues.description: The stolen diplomatic pouch concealed behind a false bottom in the Baroness's monogrammed trunk.
clues.insight: Unambiguous physical possession of the stolen diplomatic dispatch.

motive: To destroy sensitive trade treaty clauses that would bankrupt her railway holdings.
method: Exploited the tunnel darkness, vaulted the saloon partition, and extracted the pouch with her cane.
opportunity: Her booth adjoined the diplomat's partition, providing immediate reach in the darkness.

deduction.conclusion: Cushion impressions show the occupant of Booth 3 vaulted the partition during the blackout.
Cane tip abrasions on the luggage rack connect the Baroness directly to reaching the bag.
The recovered pouch inside her trunk proves the Baroness orchestrated the theft.

timeline.event: Train enters the tunnel and the blackout commences.
The Baroness uses her cane to hook the diplomat's dispatch pouch.
The Baroness slips back into Booth 3 before lighting is restored.

hints.text: Examine saloon seating upholstery for signs of physical movement in the dark.
Inspect luggage compartments for unique marks left by personal accessories.
Search private travel trunks for concealed double compartments.
